**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject every recognized foreign-currency marker**

Reject the full foreign-currency vocabulary here, not only this abbreviated list. Values such as `四万元港幣`, `新台币1000元`, or `加拿大元1000元` currently normalize to exact RMB amounts, so `canonicalMonetaryExpression` equates them with RMB gold labels. Although source review later removes the calculation amount, `assessCase` scores the accepted representation itself, causing both raw and accepted experiment metrics to award false true positives for foreign-currency predictions.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Collapse nested spans from the same anchored event**

Treat overlapping equivalent spans in the same uniquely located quote as one event. For example, if the model emits otherwise identical candidates with values `人民币四万元` and `四万元` from one quote, both normalize to `40000.00` but receive different `sourceLocation` ranges and are retained. This reintroduces duplicate candidates for a single fact and produces an extra false positive in the event-based scorer, while still allowing genuinely separate occurrences at distinct non-overlapping positions.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject qualified prefixes before a matched amount**

Do not accept a valid numeric suffix when the preceding text changes its semantics. Inputs such as `数十万元` and `几十万元` currently match the internal `十万元` token and become exact `100000.00`, while `负数四万元` matches `四万元` and becomes positive `40000.00`; the boundary check only examines the final character before the token, and the candidate-level checks inspect outside the entire value, so neither layer corrects these cases. This makes approximate or explicitly negative evidence exact and also lets the scorer equate it with a positive RMB gold amount.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not treat lexical 元 and 圆 as currency units**

Require `元` or `圆` to occur in a monetary context before classifying the value as monetary. A model-produced money candidate such as `2024年元月工资`, `元月份工资`, or `元旦工资` currently takes this branch solely because it contains `元`, so runtime ingestion accepts it instead of applying the new no-amount rejection used for `2024年7月工资`; unrelated text such as `圆满完成工资发放` is affected similarly. These candidates remain visible with `amount: null` and distort accepted/rejected coverage even though they contain no monetary expression.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve ranges whose second endpoint repeats the currency**

When a range repeats an explicit currency marker, such as a candidate value `人民币3万元` inside `人民币3万元至人民币4万元`, the suffix check does not recognize the range because it requires a numeral immediately after `至`. The candidate consequently remains `exact` with amount `30000.00`, and the later source review also accepts it, allowing a cropped range endpoint to become a usable exact amount. Permit RMB markers between the range connector and the second endpoint.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict event containment to permitted value expansions**

A candidate can use an entire narrative paragraph as its `value` and still receive a true positive merely because that span contains the event anchor. For example, `王甲声称公司长期拖欠其工资，现要求支付4000元并追究责任。` normalizes to `4000.00`, aligns with the `4000元` anchor through this containment branch, and receives a TP in all six raw/accepted modes despite violating the amount-fragment contract. Limit super-spans to the explicitly permitted currency, noun, or date-boundary expansions rather than accepting arbitrary text around an anchor.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exempt relative wage months from rate detection**

The calendar exemption only recognizes a digit or Chinese numeral before `月工资`, so ordinary wage-period phrases such as `王甲上月工资1000元`, `本月工资1000元`, or `下月工资1000元` are classified as monthly-rate contexts. A non-rate candidate for the explicit `1000元` is therefore downgraded to `rate_unit_mismatch` with `amount: null`, even when its `period` correctly names that relative month. Treat the relative-month words supported by the extraction prompt as calendar boundaries as well.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve duplicates whose source position is ambiguous**

When an otherwise identical quote occurs multiple times, both candidates have `occurrence === null`, but this fallback still treats matching fallback data as proof that they are duplicates. For example, two `四万元` candidates against `第一次支付四万元。第二次支付四万元。` are both source-ambiguous and could represent the two distinct payments, yet the second is rejected. Only collapse candidates when a unique overlapping occurrence was established; ambiguous observations need to remain available for review.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject no-amount descriptions for every supported relative month**

The relative-period vocabulary here omits forms that the new source-rate logic explicitly supports, including `这个月`, `这月`, `当月`, `该月`, `上个月`, and `下一个月`. Consequently, a model-produced money candidate such as `这个月工资` is classified as `undetermined` rather than `not_monetary`, so runtime ingestion accepts it despite there being no amount or unknown-amount marker. **<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Restrict nested deduplication to permitted amount wrappers**

Fresh evidence in runtime ingestion shows that this containment test considers any exact-value super-span equivalent to its nested amount, without applying the scorer's finite-wrapper restriction. If the model emits `王甲声称公司应支付四万元工资` before a valid `四万元` candidate with the same attributes, the latter is rejected and only the narrative value remains; the corrected event scorer then refuses to align that narrative value, turning a valid accepted prediction into a false negative based solely on output order. Limit containment deduplication to the permitted currency/noun wrappers, or retain the valid minimal span.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not discard multipliers attached to the matched amount**

When a multiplier follows the monetary token, this replacement removes it as though it were an unrelated count. Consequently, `normalizeMoneyValueV4('四万元的2倍')` returns `exact` with `40000.00`, even though the expression requires arithmetic and must not be represented by its base operand. Preserve unrelated counts such as headcounts, but classify an attached `倍` expression as unsupported rather than exposing the wrong exact amount.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject source currencies separated by attribution words**

Fresh evidence in the current tree shows that a minimal `四万元` candidate from `王甲的工资以港币支付四万元` is accepted with `amount: "40000.00"` and `status: "exact"`. This guard recognizes only currency markers directly adjoining the amount, so ordinary attribution phrases such as `港币工资四万元`, `工资以港币支付四万元`, and `港币计价工资四万元` bypass it; the new lowercase-Chinese parser then represents a foreign-currency value as exact RMB. Extend the anchored check to finite same-event currency-attribution wording without crossing clause boundaries.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recognize rate labels before accepting lowercase totals**

With the newly supported lowercase amount, a mislabeled total candidate for `四万元` in `王甲月工资标准为四万元`, `王甲月薪标准：四万元`, or `王甲每月基本工资四万元` now survives this source-unit check as exact `40000.00`. `sourceRateUnit` only permits a short list of tokens immediately after `月工资`/`月薪`, so common rate words such as `标准`, `基本`, and `约定为` prevent it from detecting the monthly rate and applying `rate_unit_mismatch`. Extend the finite rate-prefix grammar to cover these explicit wage-standard constructions while retaining the calendar-month exemptions.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Terminate the whole Worker process tree before restarting**

The built-in restart scenario calls this helper and proceeds as soon as the Wrangler parent emits `exit`, but `child.kill()` signals only that parent and does not establish that its launcher/workerd descendants have closed. The cancellation runner changed in this same commit uses a detached process group and waits for `close` specifically because parent exit can precede descendant teardown; here, a surviving descendant can keep the disposable D1 state or Wrangler sockets active while the next Worker starts, making the required HTTP regression flaky and allowing final cleanup to report success with an orphan still running. Apply the same process-group and close-wait teardown to this runner.
